mega-mania.known_source_limitations: This is a usable third-party reference, not a verified original rulebook or an authoritative correction of all rules. The English reference visibly repeats pedway text under its base Mega-way heading, omits the structural-damage defeat-point entry found in the Italian translation, and has apparent copied/garbled bat-suit and demo-charge wording. The Italian translation also combines base and expansion rules and does not include the separately referenced Blockers Manual. Differences in detailed scoring, combat order and movement wording are not silently reconciled. Original publisher rules should govern these details. The selected Italian setup/endgame text is separately attributed and retained in its original language, not presented as English or official translation. The optional, explicitly untested more-than-four-player MEGA MEGA-MANIA section is excluded. Happy Hour is a separate expansion bundled in the current reprint, not the named 1987 Mega-Mania scope; no Happy Hour coverage is claimed.
mega-mania.evidence: Complete unchanged eight-page English Esoteric Order of Gamers / Peter Universal Head Gifford Block Mania reference, v1.1 December2021, explicitly identifying Games Workshop1987 and including Mega-Mania. Operative PDF pages4-8 were read; original pages5 and8 visually checked. Pages1-3 are cover/promotion/attribution; pages6-8 print two identical copies, so only each left half is selected after exact text equality checks. Covers base setup and counters, command/deployment/activation/movement, defensive fire, attacks, fire/collapse, special units/equipment/locations, Mania and Justice effects, endgame and defeat-point ranking. Page8 supplies the missing expansion-specific 3/4-player setup: remove12/6cards, shared hardware/armoury pools, turn/board order, wraparound movement and shooting, skyrail/mega-way/flying access, multiplayer defensive fire and four-Klegg limit. A separately attributed Italian Goblin2002 translation is retained unchanged as a comparison component; selected section3 on PDF pages3-4 and section12 on PDF page11 independently corroborate setup counts and continuing Justice endgame. PDF page11 visually checked. The actual current publisher product page confirms Richard Halliwell, two additional block boards, up to four players and separate Happy Hour bundling; its inspected public links contain no rule download. Earlier publisher URL redirects to a collection, not a manual. This is a usable third-party reference, not a verified original rulebook or an authoritative correction of all rules. The English reference visibly repeats pedway text under its base Mega-way heading, omits the structural-damage defeat-point entry found in the Italian translation, and has apparent copied/garbled bat-suit and demo-charge wording. The Italian translation also combines base and expansion rules and does not include the separately referenced Blockers Manual. Differences in detailed scoring, combat order and movement wording are not silently reconciled. Original publisher rules should govern these details. The selected Italian setup/endgame text is separately attributed and retained in its original language, not presented as English or official translation. The optional, explicitly untested more-than-four-player MEGA MEGA-MANIA section is excluded. Happy Hour is a separate expansion bundled in the current reprint, not the named 1987 Mega-Mania scope; no Happy Hour coverage is claimed. Both references explicitly agree that Mania-deck exhaustion STARTS the Justice stage and play continues until the last blocker is removed or all blocks collapse. This supports a specific summary MAJOR finding only; no full summary audit, PASS, source-error adjudication or summary-body repair.
